newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Government says poverty rises in Buenos Aires.
newsitem.headline: Government says poverty rises in Buenos Aires.

text.p: The proportion of people in the Buenos Aires metropolitan area living below the poverty line rose to 27.9 percent in October 1996, according to government data Friday.

This incidence of poverty -- defined as incomes below the level necessary to pay for food and basic services -- compared with a rate of 24.8 percent in October 1995 and 19.0 percent in October 1994, according to the Economy Ministry.
Some 20.1 percent of Buenos Aires households were scraping by below the poverty line in October 1996, compared to 18.2 percent in October 1995 and 14.2 percent in October 1994.

The proportion of households living in extreme poverty -- defined as below the level of income necessary to buy enough food to live on -- was 5.5 percent. This was up from 4.8 percent in October 1995 and 3.0 percent in October 1994.
About 11.5 million people, a third of all Argentines, live in Buenos Aires.
